elements.markdown: You observed recommended directions already selected and expanded before you chose anything. We have not run the tests below. A useful hypothesis is that recommendation, selection and expansion have become coupled; the tests separate those states and then trace their effect on submission.

elements.disclosure: Inspect the proposed behavior without choosing an investigation

elements.markdown: Proposed behavior: recommendations show their reasons while exploratory directions start unselected. Selecting a direction exposes its follow-ups, and several selected directions can stay visible together. Opening this preview changes only its expansion; it does not select a direction. Closing a disclosure preserves its child answers. Deselecting a direction hides its branch, whose answers should then be omitted from submission. Whether answers are restored when that direction is selected again needs a test; it is not an observed result.

reveals.markdown: Your selections define tests and evidence to collect. Submitting this form chooses the investigation scope; it does not report that any test has passed or failed. The next step is to run the selected cases and collect the selected observations.

elements.check: Include a paired comparison of closed disclosure versus deselected branch

reveals.markdown: Use the same child answer in two fresh runs. In one run close only the disclosure; in the other deselect the direction. Capture the final UI and submitted result in both. This isolates visual collapse from semantic hiding: the closed disclosure should retain the field in the result, while the deselected branch should omit it.
